subtopics.title: Glasgow 2026 at a glance
subtopics.summary: The 23rd Commonwealth Games were held in Glasgow, Scotland, from 23 July to 2 August 2026, bringing together 74 nations and territories. The event featured 10 sports, and its mascot Finnie was inspired by Scotland's National Animal. India's flag bearer at the Closing Ceremony was Jaismine Lamboria, and India takes over hosting rights for the 2030 Games in Ahmedabad.

subtopics.title: History and evolution of the Games
subtopics.summary: The idea of a Commonwealth-wide sporting competition can be traced to the 1911 Inter-Empire Championships in London. The first Games were held in 1930 in Canada under the name British Empire Games. The event was officially renamed Commonwealth Games in 1978, and it is organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation.
facts: Idea traced to the 1911 Inter-Empire Championships, London, part of the Festival of Empire during King George V's coronation celebrations

subtopics.title: India's medal performance at Glasgow 2026
subtopics.summary: India won 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze) and finished 4th on the medal tally, behind Australia, England and Canada. This was fewer than the 61 medals India won at Birmingham 2022. The booklet links the lower count to a reduced contingent and to the absence of several traditional medal-producing disciplines.

subtopics.title: Notable Indian achievements
subtopics.summary: Several Indian athletes produced historic results at Glasgow 2026. Five women boxers won gold, and Mirabai Chanu became the first Indian weightlifter to win three consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medals. Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallists in judo, and Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw.

quizzes.passage:
Scotland is set to host the Commonwealth Games for the fourth time, after earlier editions in Edinburgh and Glasgow. The 2026 edition was staged in Glasgow and brought together athletes from the nations and territories of the Commonwealth. The Games are organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation, and the event has a long history that began with a sporting competition held in London in 1911. Glasgow had hosted the event once before, in 2014, so the city has welcomed the Games previously.

The programme for 2026 covered a wide range of disciplines, including athletics, swimming, cycling, weightlifting, boxing and judo. Teams from many countries took part, although not every nation entered every discipline. India's contingent included para athletes, and its medal count was reported at the close of the event. Indian women boxers were among the standout performers of the event, and several of them won gold medals.

At the closing ceremony, India's flag was carried by boxer Jaismine Lamboria, who had won a gold medal in the women's 57 kg category. The Commonwealth Flag is handed over to the next host at the end of each edition, which marks the beginning of preparations for the following Games. Medal tallies are widely reported, and they are a common way to compare how countries performed across the event.

quizzes.passage:
The idea of a sporting contest across the Commonwealth is older than the Games themselves. It can be traced to an event held in London in 1911, which formed part of a Festival of Empire organised during the coronation celebrations of King George V. The first edition of the Games was held in 1930 in a Canadian city, and the concept is credited to a sportswriter from the same country. The event was generally held once every four years, although the editions scheduled for 1942 and 1946 did not take place.

Over the decades the event has carried several different titles, and its name has changed more than once. Today the Games are organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation, and each edition is hosted by a nation chosen in advance. India has hosted the Games, and its best performance at the Games, with 101 medals, came at that edition.

A centenary edition of the Games is planned for India in a future year, which will mark one hundred years since the first Games. India's first participation came decades before it hosted the Games, showing a long link with the event. The Games are a multi-sport event in which athletes from many nations compete for medals across a range of sports.
